text: Making the stake captive closes the release leak but does not rescue the instrument: the surviving capacity slope is still negative in the carry cost because the walk value of the balance cancels through the surplus — the stake never mints a hostage.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Refundable Stake Does Not Expand Deterrent Capacity in Long-Lived Delegation: Collateral, Premia, and Pseudonymous Markets (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7322599

isBasedOn.name: Refundable Stake Does Not Expand Deterrent Capacity in Long-Lived Delegation: Collateral, Premia, and Pseudonymous Markets

abstract: Captivity does not rescue the instrument: when misconduct is punishable in place with the stake seized before any release clock runs, the leak closes, but the surviving slope is −p CF , because the walk value of the balance cancels through the surplus. The stake never mints a hostage.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: misconduct punishable in place with stake seized before any release clock runs
